caption_verbatim: Measurements relevant to platybasia and basilar invagination and an example of basilar invagination on CT. The base of skull angle is measured by drawing a line from the nasion to the center of the pituitary fossa and another line from the pituitary fossa to the anterior edge of the foramen magnum (A). The Chamberlain line extends from the posterior edge of the hard palate to the tip of the opisthion (dotted line). The McGregor line extends from the posterior edge of the hard palate to the most caudal aspect of the occipital bone (dotted and dashed line). Sagittal reformatted head CT image (B) shows the dens clearly above the palatosuboccipital line, or McGregor line (white line), drawn from the bony palate to the tangency plane beneath the occipital bone. There are also findings of platybasia, with flattening of the basal angle. Also visible are artifacts related to previous occipitocervical fusion posteriorly.
pointers: Panel A (grey/black line diagram): black dashed lines (two limbs) from nasion region to centre of dashed-circle pituitary fossa and from fossa to anterior edge of foramen magnum = base of skull (basal) angle; black dashed circle = pituitary fossa; black dotted line = Chamberlain line (hard palate to opisthion); black dotted-and-dashed line = McGregor line (hard palate to caudal occiput) - the two lines run nearly parallel and are hard to separate. No letters or labels for the lines inside image; panel letters A,B only. Panel B: thin white horizontal line (McGregor) lying on the very bottom edge of the crop. Panel B VERIFIED on image: brain-window sagittal CT; thin white McGregor line at bottom edge; bony dens/C1 tip visible just above it (small bright structure at lower centre), consistent with caption; posterior fusion hardware not visible in this crop (book image is itself tightly framed). Not corrupted.

caption_verbatim: Atlanto-occipital assimilation. Sagittal CT cervical spine (A) shows atlanto-occipital assimilation (black arrow), as well as assimilation of C2 and C3 (black arrowhead). Basilar invagination is evident, with the dens protruding above McGregor's line (white line). Coronal CT (B) shows the assimilation between the occipital condyles and C1 (black arrows), with obliteration of the joint space. The C2 and C3 vertebral bodies are fused (asterisk). Sagittal T1-weighted image (C) shows finding of Chiari I malformation, with cerebellar tonsillar descent (asterisk).
pointers: A: black arrow -> atlanto-occipital assimilation (top); black arrowhead -> C2-C3 assimilation (anterior vertebral body level); thin white line = McGregor line drawn from palate (left) across to occiput. B: two black arrows (left and right) -> occipital condyle-C1 fusion; white asterisk -> fused C2/C3 bodies. C: white asterisk -> cerebellar tonsils / tonsillar descent at foramen magnum. Caption and image agree; legible.
topic: congenital:atlanto-occipital assimilation; Chiari I; basilar invagination
modality: CT sagittal (A) / CT coronal (B) / MRI T1 sagittal (C)
